reference.source: Nelson Textbook of Pediatrics / Harrison's Principles of Internal Medicine
clinicalPearls: An organic acidaemia of leucine catabolism caused by deficiency of isovaleryl-CoA dehydrogenase
A distinctive odour of sweaty feet during acute episodes, from accumulated isovaleric acid, is a useful clinical clue
Acute neonatal form presents with vomiting, lethargy, poor feeding progressing to encephalopathy with high-anion-gap metabolic acidosis and ketosis
A milder chronic intermittent form presents later with recurrent episodes of vomiting and acidosis triggered by illness or protein load
Common laboratory features include acidosis, ketosis, hyperammonaemia, hypoglycaemia and cytopenias such as neutropenia and thrombocytopenia
Elevated isovalerylcarnitine (C5) on acylcarnitine profile and isovalerylglycine in urine confirm the diagnosis

Management principles are leucine (protein) restriction, and conjugation of the toxic metabolite using glycine and carnitine supplementation to enhance excretion, plus aggressive treatment of catabolism
Readily identified on newborn screening through elevated C5 acylcarnitine, allowing pre-symptomatic treatment
reference.pathophysiology: Isovaleric acidemia is an autosomal recessive defect of isovaleryl-CoA dehydrogenase, an enzyme of the leucine degradation pathway. Deficiency causes isovaleryl-CoA and its derivatives (isovaleric acid, isovalerylglycine, isovalerylcarnitine and 3-hydroxyisovaleric acid) to accumulate. Isovaleric acid is responsible for the characteristic odour and, together with the other metabolites, produces metabolic acidosis and is toxic to the central nervous system and bone marrow. Accumulated organic acids also secondarily impair the urea cycle, contributing to hyperammonaemia. Conjugation of isovaleryl-CoA with glycine and carnitine forms non-toxic, readily excreted products, which is exploited therapeutically.
additionalDifferentials: Multiple acyl-CoA dehydrogenase deficiency (glutaric aciduria type 2)
additionalInvestigations: Blood gas with anion gap, glucose, lactate and ammonia
Urine organic acids showing isovalerylglycine and 3-hydroxyisovaleric acid
Plasma acylcarnitine profile with elevated C5 (isovalerylcarnitine)
Full blood count for neutropenia and thrombocytopenia
Molecular testing of the IVD gene
redFlags: Acute metabolic decompensation with severe acidosis and encephalopathy is an emergency
Hyperammonaemia contributing to altered consciousness during crises
Sepsis-like collapse in a neonate that is actually metabolic decompensation
Severe neutropenia with risk of overwhelming infection during acute illness
reference.prognosis: With newborn screening and early treatment many patients have a favourable outcome and normal development; the chronic intermittent form is often milder, but untreated acute neonatal disease can be fatal or cause neurological damage, and outcome depends on preventing and promptly treating decompensations.
pitfalls: Missing the diagnostic sweaty-feet odour or attributing the presentation to sepsis
Neglecting glycine and carnitine conjugation therapy that enhances detoxification
Under-treating catabolic stress during intercurrent illness
Overlooking neutropenia and infection risk during acute crises
